trap.title: Arrive at or arrive to?
trap.wrong: I arrived to the office at eight.
trap.right: I arrived at the office at eight.
trap.explanation: Thai speakers often think of ถึง as 'to', so they say 'arrive to'. In English we arrive at a building or point, arrive in a city or country, and never arrive to a place.

other_language.headline: German: Punctuality Is a Form of Respect
other_language.note: In Germany, being on time is more than good manners. Many people see it as a sign that you respect other people's time. Trains are expected to run to the minute, and a meeting that starts at nine really starts at nine. If you will be even five minutes late, it is polite to send a message. Germans also tend to separate work time and free time clearly, so after-hours emails may not get a quick reply.
